arguments.code:
import json, re
cfg = json.loads(read('renovate.json'))
src = read('versions.toml')
for m in cfg['regexManagers']:
    for ms in m['matchStrings']:
        rx = re.compile(ms)
        found = False
        for line in src.splitlines():
            mt = rx.search(line)
            if mt and 'currentValue' in mt.groupdict():
                found = True
                print(f"matchString: {ms!r}")
                print(f"  line: {line.strip()}")
                print(f"  currentValue={mt['currentValue']!r} -> dep {m['depNameTemplate']} ({m['datasourceTemplate']})")
                ex = re.compile(m['extractVersion']).match(mt['currentValue'])
                print(f"  extractVersion strip: {ex.group('version') if ex else '(no match -> used as-is)'}")
                print(f"  versioning: {m['versioningTemplate']}")
        if not found:
            print(f"NO MATCH for {ms!r}")
        print()

import json, re
cfg = json.loads(read('renovate.json'))
src = read('versions.toml')
for m in cfg['regexManagers']:
    for ms in m['matchStrings']:
        rx = re.compile(ms)
        found = False
        for line in src.splitlines():
            mt = rx.search(line)
            if mt and 'currentValue' in mt.groupdict():
                found = True
                print(f"matchString: {ms!r}")
                print(f"  line: {line.strip()}")
                print(f"  currentValue={mt['currentValue']!r} -> dep {m['depNameTemplate']} ({m['datasourceTemplate']})")
                ex = re.compile(m['extractVersion']).match(mt['currentValue'])
                print(f"  extractVersion strip: {ex.group('version') if ex else '(no match -> used as-is)'}")
                print(f"  versioning: {m['versioningTemplate']}")
        if not found:
            print(f"NO MATCH for {ms!r}")
        print()

content.text:
===== v1.13.1 (2026-08-27T08:18:45Z) =====
## What's Changed
* Preserve fork checkpoints across runtime restarts by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1065
* Support one-to-one port ranges in Smolfiles and CLI mappings by @fgrehm in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1066
* Add portable live checkpoints by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1067
* Warn when a saved registry token has expired instead of surfacing a bare 401 by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1068
* Serve a browser client on the VNC port so a machine's desktop opens in any browser by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1070

## New Contributors
* @fgrehm made their first contribution in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1066

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/compare/v1.13.0...v1.13.1

===== v1.13.0 (2026-08-26T06:33:06Z) =====
## What's Changed
* Re-stage a damaged image-archive cache entry instead of trusting that the path exists by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1058
* Fail when the release lookup fails instead of falling back to a hardcoded 0.1.1 by @NickyHeC in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1059
* Ship the guest Chromium wrapper in the desktop recipes with software WebGL enabled by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1055
* Give a pack machine's first boot a start window that covers the layer unpack by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1056
* Add SECURITY.md by @NickyHeC in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/983
* Floor host loopback in the default local egress mode by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1060
* Support nested machine checkpoints by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1062
* Extract packed layers on the host when the pack predates in-guest unpacking, instead of handing its agent tars it cannot read by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1064
* Release 1.13.0 by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1063


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/compare/v1.12.0...v1.13.0

===== v1.12.0 (2026-08-24T20:37:10Z) =====
## What's Changed
* Add an opt-in virtio-gpu scanout with a host-side VNC server and virtio-input so machines can run an interactive Linux desktop by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1027
* Ship virtio-input-capable guest kernels and an input-enabled macOS libkrun by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1043
* Harden forked workloads and add transactional embedded batch forking by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1044
* Make large pack pushes reliable with upload-scoped timeouts and a chunked fallback by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1045
* Rewrite a loopback proxy host to the host's outbound address so guests can reach it by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1046
* Cut v1.12.0 with the display-capable libkrun and rebuilt platform libraries by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1048
* Harden live fork execution for rollout sandboxes by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1049
* Pack a machine created from a local image archive or rootfs directory by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1047
* Pin the Vulkan driver on exec only when the container actually has the bundle by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1052
* Bump the workspace crates to 1.12.0 so the library crates ship at the engine's version by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1051
* Mount the bundled Vulkan driver into pod and overlay containers too by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1053
* Boot a pod sandbox with a virtio-gpu device when the pod asks for one by @BinSquare in https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/pull/1054


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/compare/v1.11.1...v1.12.0

===== v1.11.1 (2026-08-24T04:17:54Z) =====

Since the pin (`1.8.2`, 2026-08-15) smolvm shipped **12 releases** (v1.8.3 → v1.13.1, all stable). Grouped by theme, with the release each landed in:

## Networking
- **Named inter-VM networks** with routed addressing between machines (1.8.3)
- `host.smolvm.internal` resolves to the gateway; default `/etc/hosts` when the image ships none (1.8.3)
- Loopback proxy host rewritten to the host's outbound address so guests can reach it (1.12.0)
- Guest IPv6 gated on real host reachability, resolver defaulted **IPv4-first** (1.10.1)
- libkrunfw guest kernel with **IPv4/IPv6 policy routing** — TUN-based VPN/proxy clients work (1.10.1)
- Guest TCP FIN forwarded properly in the virtio-net relay (1.8.3)

## Remote volumes / S3
- `--volume` can mount **S3 and any rclone remote** (1.10.0/1.10.1); agent mounts S3 natively, no rclone needed in the image (1.10.1)
- Remote volumes carried on every exec, on the embedded machine spec (SDK machines), and on ephemeral runs without a persistent overlay (1.11.0/1.11.1)

## Packing / image fidelity
- Default `/etc/hosts` provided (1.8.3); **auto-shrink disk by reclaiming freed blocks to the host** (1.9.0)
- Disk auto-grows an existing storage/overlay to the requested size instead of booting the stale one (1.9.2) — relevant to preloop's storage sizing
- Archive-flatten scratch staged on the storage disk instead of guest tmpfs; damaged layer caches rebuilt from the source artifact (1.9.1/1.9.2)
- Pack-export reads get one consistent ceiling (1.8.3 — yours); pre-1.13 packs extracted host-side when they predate in-guest unpacking (1.13.0)

## Forking / checkpoints
- Forkable golden survives config-change VM restarts; keep-alive container reused for fork-clone exec instead of a fresh container per call (1.9.1)
- **Transactional embedded batch forking**, hardened forked workloads (1.12.0); **nested machine checkpoints** (1.13.0); **portable live checkpoints** and fork checkpoints preserved across runtime restarts (1.13.1)

## GPU / display
- Segmented CUDA graph capture (1.9.0); automatic CUDA replay + distributed multi-GPU (1.9.2)
- Bundled Venus Vulkan driver injected into GPU workload containers; driver pinned only when the container has the bundle; mounted into pod/overlay containers too (1.9.0/1.12.0)
- **Opt-in virtio-gpu scanout + VNC** with virtio-input — interactive Linux desktop; VNC port now serves a browser client (1.12.0/1.13.1)

## Reliability / platform
- Broken blob downloads resume with bound retry instead of hanging machine create (1.10.1)
- Release lookup **fails instead of falling back to hardcoded 0.1.1** (1.13.0); expired registry-token warning instead of bare 401 (1.13.1)
- macOS: `libkrun.dylib` Homebrew refs relocated to `@loader_path` so packed launchers boot (1.9.2); missing hypervisor entitlement named on boot -22 (1.9.0 — yours); net-enabled libkrun restored (1.8.0); aarch64-KVM snapshot + fork support (1.9.2)
- Windows krun.dll rebuilt so machines boot on WHP again (1.10.1)
- Egress policy enforced even when served from the image cache; egress denials recorded per machine (1.9.0/1.8.1)
- cgroup2 controllers delegated at agent boot; unknown fields rejected on exec/run API (1.9.0/1.9.2); h2 bumped to clear RUSTSEC-2026-0258 (1.9.0)

## Worth flagging for preloop
- **1.9.2's `@loader_path` relocation** — `preloop update --ensure-runtime` on macOS installs "latest stable ≥ 1.8.1"; packed-launcher boot was broken before 1.9.2, so the floor's minimum is fine but the runtime floor comment ("first release satisfying all invariants") predates it.
- 1.13.0's fail-fast release lookup is a behavior preloop's `--ensure-runtime` interacts with (no silent 0.1.1 fallback).
- Your own PRs shipped in this window: pack-export read ceiling (1.8.3), macOS entitlement message (1.9.0), flatten EAGAIN window + post-`--` option validation + storage disk grow (1.9.2), mount-socket collision fix (1.8.0).

The renovate bump would go 1.8.2 → **1.13.1**; the smolvm-release-verify E2E gate exists precisely because the disk-grow and egress changes touch preloop's VM lifecycle.

---
name: preloop-submit-before-push
description: "In the preloop repo, default to submitting workflows to the preloop server and opening draft PRs instead of push-and-wait-for-webhook; dependency bump PRs belong to Renovate, not the agent"
condition: ["git\\s+push", "gh\\s+pr\\s+create", "preloop-runner-client.*submit", "api/v1/runs"]
scope: "tool:bash"
---

When working in the preloop repo (or any repo whose CI runs on the preloop
control plane), the default is to drive checks through the preloop server
directly, not to push a branch and wait for the GitHub webhook to reach it.

Before pushing a branch or creating a PR:

1. **Submit the workflow to the preloop server first** — this is the
   push-to-server path, and it runs the checks without the webhook round
   trip:
   ```sh
   PRELOOP_SYSTEM_TOKEN=<token> \
     cargo run -p preloop-runner-client -- --server <server> submit \
     -W <workflow.yml> --workspace-root <repo> --repository <owner/repo>
   ```
   `<server>` is the preloop control plane (e.g. `https://aksh.preloop.dev`
   or `http://127.0.0.1:9090` for a local `just serve`); the native API
   token comes from the server's `AKSH_SYSTEM_TOKEN`/`PRELOOP_SYSTEM_TOKEN`
   (local default: `preloop-system-token`). Equivalently, `POST
   /api/v1/runs` with the workflow YAML. This also snapshots the local
   workspace so reusable workflows and the submitted file resolve against
   the current tree.

2. **Create PRs as drafts** (`gh pr create --draft`) unless the user asks
   for a ready PR, and show the full title/body in chat before creating
   (see ts-show-before-create).

3. **Never draft dependency-bump PRs yourself.** Runner (`runner_version`)
   and SmolVM (`smolvm_golden_version`) bumps are Renovate's job — it opens
   the PR once `renovate.json` is on the default branch and the app is
   installed, and the verify/sync workflows gate it. Hand-simulating those
   PRs is a failure; leave them to the bot.

Push-and-wait-for-webhook is the fallback for when the preloop server is
not the target (e.g. GitHub-hosted-only repos), not the default.

- name: Build Preloop CLI
        run: |
          cargo build --release -p preloop-cli -p preloop-runner-server

      - name: Build Linux runner bundle
        run: |
          cargo zigbuild --release \
            --target "$RUNNER_TARGET" \
            -p preloop-runner

      - name: Install compatible smolvm
        env:
          SMOLVM_VERSION: "1.8.2"
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The verified golden release, pinned in versions.toml and bumped
          # by Renovate; smolvm-release-verify.yml gates the bump.
          SMOLVM_VERSION="$(grep '^smolvm_golden_version' versions.toml | cut -d'"' -f2)"
          [ -n "$SMOLVM_VERSION" ] || { echo "smolvm_golden_version missing from versions.toml" >&2; exit 1; }
          ARCHIVE="smolvm-${SMOLVM_VERSION}-darwin-arm64.tar.gz"
          BASE="https://github.com/smol-machines/smolvm/releases/download/v${SMOLVM_VERSION}"
          curl -fsSL -o "$ARCHIVE" "$BASE/$ARCHIVE"
          curl -fsSL -o checksums.sha256 "$BASE/checksums.sha256"
          grep -F "$ARCHIVE" checksums.sha256 | shasum -a 256 -c -
          tar -xzf "$ARCHIVE"
          SRC="smolvm-${SMOLVM_VERSION}-darwin-arm64"
          mkdir -p "$HOME/.smolvm"
          rm -rf "$HOME/.smolvm/lib"
          cp -R "$SRC/lib" "$HOME/.smolvm/lib"
…
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

name: ci
permissions:
  contents: read

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Keep push-triggered checks observable while the self-hosted pool boots.
  pull_request:
    # Docs-only PRs must not burn pool time: skip when every changed file
    # is a markdown document.
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
  schedule:
    # Nightly intensive property profile at 02:00 UTC
    - cron: "0 2 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      profile:
        description: "Property profile: fast (default) or intensive"
        required: false
        default: "fast"


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Property-test CI notes
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PR / push: fast profile — 256 cases for pure/model/runner, 64 for HTTP.
# Scheduled / manual intensive: release mode, 10k cases, 100k shrink iters.
#
# The regular Linux jobs never run live GitHub or privileged official-runner
# probes. `runner-conformance.yml` runs the privileged deep runner probe on the
# dedicated smolVM self-hosted pool for every pull request.
# The differential harness dry-run (credential-free) runs in both profiles.
#
# Sleep-guard: each property-test job mechanically scans new test files for
# `sleep(` and fails the build if any match is found.
#
# Zero-filter guard: `cargo test -- --list | grep <filter>` must return at
# least one test name before case-count runs are launched.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

sources.title: Repository Webhooks | GitHub API
sources.snippet:
The Repository Webhooks API allows repository admins to manage the post-receive hooks for a repository.
Topic URLs for a GitHub repository’s pushes are in this format: ... The event can be any event string that is listed at the top of this document. The default format is what existing post-receive hooks should expect: A JSON body sent as the payload parameter in a POST. You can also specify to receive the raw JSON body with either an Accept header, or a .json extension. Accept: application/json https://github.com/:owner/:repo/events/push.json
Note: Repository service hooks (like email or Campfire) can have at most one configured at a time. Creating hooks for a service that already has one configured will update the existing hook. Repositories can have multiple webhooks installed. Each webhook should have a unique config.
This will trigger the hook with the latest push to the current repository if the hook is subscribed to push events. If the hook is not subscribed to push events, the server will respond with 204 but no test POST will be generated. ... This will trigger a ping event to be sent to the hook. ... In order for GitHub to send webhook payloads, your server needs to be accessible from the Internet.

sources.title: GitHub API – Openship Docs
sources.snippet:
POST /api/github/repos/:owner/:repo/webhooks registers the Openship push webhook on the repo (or reuses an existing one) so pushes trigger auto-deploy. It takes no request body — the target repo comes from the path. GET lists the repo's hooks.
POST /api/github/repos/:owner/:repo/webhooks registers the Openship push webhook on the repo (or reuses an existing one) so pushes trigger auto-deploy. It takes no request body — the target repo comes from the path. GET lists the repo's hooks.
The GitHub API connects an Openship instance to GitHub — via the Openship GitHub App, an OAuth account, or the local gh CLI — and then lets you browse the accounts, repositories, branches and files you can deploy from. It also manages the push webhooks that drive auto-deploy. In the dashboard this is the GitHub connection card in Settings and the repo picker in the deploy wizard.
The :owner/:repo isn't visible to the active GitHub source (private, not granted to your member role, or does not exist). Confirm the repo appears in GET /api/github/home first.
Query: path (default repo root) and branch. GET /api/github/repos/:owner/:repo/file — one file's contents. Query: file (default package.json) and branch.

You can use the REST API to manage repository, organization, and app webhooks. You can list webhook deliveries for a webhook, or get and redeliver an individual delivery for a webhook, which can be integrated into an external app or service.
Repository webhooks allow you to receive HTTP POST payloads whenever certain events happen in a repository. You can use the REST API to manage repository, organization, and app webhooks. You can list webhook deliveries for a webhook, or get and redeliver an individual delivery for a webhook, which can be integrated into an external app or service.
You can also use the REST API to change the configuration of the webhook. For example, you can modify the payload URL, content type, SSL verification, and secret. For more information, see: ... If you would like to set up a single webhook to receive events from all of your organization's repositories, see our REST API documentation for Organization Webhooks.
In addition to the REST API, GitHub can also serve as a PubSubHubbub hub for repositories. In order for GitHub Enterprise Server to send webhook payloads, your server needs to be accessible from the Internet.
The default format is what existing post-receive hooks should expect: A JSON body sent as the payload parameter in a POST. You can also specify to receive the raw JSON body with either an Accept header, or a .json extension. Accept: application/json https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/events/push.json · Callback URLs can use the HTTP protocol. # Send updates to a PostBin bin https://www.toptal.com/developers/postbin/123 · The GitHub PubSubHubbub endpoint is: http(s)://HOSTNAME/api/v3/hub.

# REST API endpoints for repository webhooks

Use the REST API to create and manage webhooks for your repositories.

## About repository webhooks

Repository webhooks allow your server to receive HTTP `POST` payloads whenever certain events happen in a repository. For more information, see [Webhooks documentation](/en/webhooks).

> \[!NOTE]
> Most endpoints use `Authorization: Bearer <YOUR-TOKEN>` and `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` headers, plus `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10`. Curl examples below omit these standard headers for brevity.

## List repository webhooks

```
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks
```

Lists webhooks for a repository. last response may return null if there have not been any deliveries within 30 days.

### Parameters

#### Headers

* **`accept`** (string)
  Setting to `application/vnd.github+json` is recommended.

#### Path and query parameters

* **`owner`** (string) (required)
  The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

* **`repo`** (string) (required)
  The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

* **`per_page`** (integer)
  The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "Using pagination in the REST API."
  Default: `30`

* **`page`** (integer)
  The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "Using pagination in the REST API."
  Default: `1`

### HTTP response status codes

* **200** - OK

* **404** - Resource not found

### Code examples

#### Example

**Request:**

```curl
curl -L \
  -X GET \
  https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/hooks
```

**Response schema (Status: 200):**

Array of `Webhook`:

* `type`: required, string
* `id`: required, integer
* `name`: required, string
* `active`: required, boolean
* `events`: required, array of string
* `config`: required, `Webhook Configuration`:
  * `url`: string, format: uri
  * `content_type`: string
  * `secret`: string
  * `insecure_ssl`: one of:
    * **string**
    * **number**
* `updated_at`: required, string, format: date-time
* `created_at`: required, string, format: date-time
* `url`: required, string, format: uri
* `test_url`: required, string, format: uri
* `ping_url`: required, string, format: uri
* `deliveries_url`: string, format: uri
* `last_response`: required, `Hook Response`:
  * `code`: required, integer or null
  * `status`: required, string or null
  * `message`: required, string or null

## Create a repository webhook

```
POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks
```

Repositories can have multiple webhooks installed. Each webhook should have a unique config. Multiple webhooks can
share the same config as long as those webhooks do not have any events that overlap.

### Parameters

#### Headers

* **`accept`** (string)
  Setting to `application/vnd.github+json` is recommended.

#### Path and query parameters

* **`owner`** (string) (required)
  The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

* **`repo`** (string) (required)
  The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

#### Body parameters

* **`name`** (string)
  Use web to create a webhook. Default: web. This parameter only accepts the value web.

* **`config`** (object)
  Key/value pairs to provide settings for this webhook.
  * **`url`** (string)
    The URL to which the payloads will be delivered.
  * **`content_type`** (string)
    The media type used to serialize the payloads. Supported values include json and form. The default is form.
  * **`secret`** (string)
    If provided, the secret will be used as the key to generate the HMAC hex digest value for delivery signature headers.
  * **`insecure_ssl`** (string or number)
    Determines whether the SSL certificate of the host for url will be verified when delivering payloads. Supported values include 0 (verification is performed) and 1 (verification is not performed). The default is 0. We strongly recommend not setting this to 1 as you are subject to man-in-the-middle and other attacks.

* **`events`** (array of strings)
  Determines what events the hook is triggered for.
  Default: `push`

* **`active`** (boolean)
  Determines if notifications are sent when the webhook is triggered. Set to true to send notifications.
  Default: `true`

### HTTP response status codes

* **201** - Created

* **403** - Forbidden

* **404** - Resource not found

* **422** - Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.

### Code examples

#### Example

**Request:**

```curl
curl -L \
  -X POST \
  https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/hooks \
  -d '{
  "name": "web",
  "active": true,
  "events": [
    "push",
    "pull_request"
  ],
  "config": {
    "url": "https://example.com/webhook",
    "content_type": "json",
    "insecure_ssl": "0"
  }
}'
```

**Response schema (Status: 201):**

* `type`: required, string
* `id`: required, integer
* `name`: required, string
* `active`: required, boolean
* `events`: required, array of string
* `config`: required, `Webhook Configuration`:
  * `url`: string, format: uri
  * `content_type`: string
  * `secret`: string
  * `insecure_ssl`: one of:
    * **string**
    * **number**
* `updated_at`: required, string, format: date-time
* `created_at`: required, string, format: date-time
* `url`: required, string, format: uri
* `test_url`: required, string, format: uri
* `ping_url`: required, string, format: uri
* `deliveries_url`: string, format: uri
* `last_response`: required, `Hook Response`:
  * `code`: required, integer or null
  * `status`: required, string or null
  * `message`: required, string or null

## Get a repository webhook

```
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}
```

Returns a webhook configured in a repository. To get only the webhook config properties, see "Get a webhook configuration for a repository."

### Parameters

#### Headers

* **`accept`** (string)
  Setting to `application/vnd.github+json` is recommended.

#### Path and query parameters

* **`owner`** (string) (required)
  The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

* **`repo`** (string) (required)
  The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

* **`hook_id`** (integer) (required)
  The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the X-GitHub-Hook-ID header of a webhook delivery.

### HTTP response status codes

* **200** - OK

* **404** - Resource not found

### Code examples

#### Example

**Request:**

```curl
curl -L \
  -X GET \
  https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/hooks/HOOK_ID
```

**Response schema (Status: 200):**

Same response schema as [Create a repository webhook](#create-a-repository-webhook).

## Update a repository webhook

```
PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}
```

Updates a webhook configured in a repository. If you previously had a secret set, you must provide the same secret or set a new secret or the secret will be removed. If you are only updating individual webhook config properties, use "Update a webhook configuration for a repository."

### Parameters

#### Headers

* **`accept`** (string)
  Setting to `application/vnd.github+json` is recommended.

#### Path and query parameters

* **`owner`** (string) (required)
  The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

* **`repo`** (string) (required)
  The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

* **`hook_id`** (integer) (required)
  The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the X-GitHub-Hook-ID header of a webhook delivery.

#### Body parameters

* **`config`** (object)
  Configuration object of the webhook
  * **`url`** (string)
    The URL to which the payloads will be delivered.
  * **`content_type`** (string)
    The media type used to serialize the payloads. Supported values include json and form. The default is form.
  * **`secret`** (string)
    If provided, the secret will be used as the key to generate the HMAC hex digest value for delivery signature headers.
  * **`insecure_ssl`** (string or number)
    Determines whether the SSL certificate of the host for url will be verified when delivering payloads. Supported values include 0 (verification is performed) and 1 (verification is not performed). The default is 0. We strongly recommend not setting this to 1 as you are subject to man-in-the-middle and other attacks.

* **`events`** (array of strings)
  Determines what events the hook is triggered for. This replaces the entire array of events.
  Default: `push`

* **`add_events`** (array of strings)
  Determines a list of events to be added to the list of events that the Hook triggers for.

* **`remove_events`** (array of strings)
  Determines a list of events to be removed from the list of events that the Hook triggers for.

* **`active`** (boolean)

If the Renovate app had been granted `preloop`, GitHub would have **registered a webhook on the repo instantly** (that's the only way a hosted app receives PR/push events). There is none. The repo's only webhook anywhere in the org is a `web` hook on `runner-image-blobs` — every other repo, `preloop` included, has zero. So the app is **still not granted this repo**.

- Permissions are full: `contents`, `pull_requests`, `issues`, `checks`, `statuses`, `workflows` all write
- `updated_at: 2026-08-28T12:32:34` — so your save **did** register on the install record today

That combination (install touched today, permissions fine, but no repo webhook) points to the repo grant not landing on the right place.

## How to find it (30 seconds, no picture needed)

Where you "configured it" must be the **`preloopdev` org** installation, not your personal account:

3. Save, then check the repo: `preloop` → **Settings → Webhooks** → there must be an entry named **Renovate**

That last check is definitive — if a "Renovate" webhook exists on `preloop`, it's connected (and I'll see the branch/PR within the hour). If it's not there, the grant either went to a different account, a different repo, or wasn't saved.

The exact root cause was a **schema validation error in `renovate.json`** that caused Renovate to abort every run on this repo before extracting any dependencies or opening PRs.

### Why it failed

Running `renovate-config-validator` and the Renovate engine locally on `renovate.json` caught the exact error:

```text
INFO: Found renovate config errors
  - topic: "Configuration Error"
  - message: "Custom Manager contains disallowed fields: extractVersion"
INFO: Repository has invalid config
  - validationError: "The renovate configuration file contains some invalid settings"
```

1. **`extractVersion` vs `extractVersionTemplate`**: Renovate's regex manager schema requires `extractVersionTemplate`, not `extractVersion`.
2. **`regexManagers` vs `customManagers`**: Renovate migrated `regexManagers` to `customManagers` with `customType: "regex"`.

Because `extractVersion` was rejected as a disallowed field, the Renovate worker failed configuration validation and silently exited without opening any PRs or creating the Dependency Dashboard.

---

### The Fix

`renovate.json` has been updated and validated cleanly (`INFO: Config validated successfully`):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": ["config:recommended"],
  "dependencyDashboard": true,
  "packageRules": [
    {
      "matchDatasources": ["github-releases"],
      "matchDepNames": ["actions/runner", "smol-machines/smolvm"],
      "labels": ["dependencies"]
    },
    {
      "matchDatasources": ["github-releases"],
      "matchDepNames": ["smol-machines/smolvm"],
      "description": "SmolVM bumps auto-merge once ci.yml and the smolvm-release-verify check pass.",
      "automerge": true,
      "automergeType": "pr"
    },
    {
      "matchDatasources": ["github-releases"],
      "matchDepNames": ["actions/runner"],
      "description": "Runner bump PR is the tripwire for the runner-watch pipeline.",
      "labels": ["protocol-sync", "dependencies"]
    }
  ],
  "customManagers": [
    {
      "customType": "regex",
      "description": "Official actions/runner release pin in versions.toml.",
      "fileMatch": ["^versions\\.toml$"],
      "matchStrings": ["runner_version\\s*=\\s*\"(?<currentValue>[^\"]+)\""],
      "depNameTemplate": "actions/runner",
      "datasourceTemplate": "github-releases",
      "versioningTemplate": "semver",
      "extractVersionTemplate": "^v(?<version>.*)$"
    },
    {
      "customType": "regex",
      "description": "SmolVM release the golden workflow builds with.",
      "fileMatch": ["^versions\\.toml$"],
      "matchStrings": ["smolvm_golden_version\\s*=\\s*\"(?<currentValue>[^\"]+)\""],
      "depNameTemplate": "smol-machines/smolvm",
      "datasourceTemplate": "github-releases",
      "versioningTemplate": "semver",

}
```

name: runner-sync

# Drives the runner-watch pipeline for a new official actions/runner release.
#
# Renovate's runner_version bump PR (labeled protocol-sync) is the tripwire.
# This workflow reconciles it:
#   prep (hosted, every PR): diff + triage the upstream delta and post the
#     spec summary on the tripwire PR, so the change surface is reviewable
#     immediately.
#   sync (self-hosted, opt-in): implement/review (when agents are enabled),
#     record-golden (official bytes via mitmproxy), conform (replay against
#     the built server), and open the tiered draft PRs, each tagged
#     protocol-sync + priority:{critical,high,low} (see the `pr` command).
#     The runner_version bump and pipeline artifacts land on a
#     runner-sync/v<version> branch; the tiered PRs are based on it.
#
# The sync job is inert until a runner-sync host exists (mitmproxy + official
# runner + Rust toolchain + gh) and RUNNER_SYNC_HOST_WORKSPACE is set — the
# same opt-in pattern as conformance.yml, so nothing queues forever. Agent
# stages run only when RUNNER_SYNC_AGENTS=true and the agent CLIs (codex,
# claude) are installed on the host; otherwise triage ships specs for human
# implementation, which the tiered PRs surface.

on:
  pull_request:
    # Only Renovate's bump PRs (and the rare human versions.toml change)

content.text:
**Yes, exactly.** Renovate acts as the **tripwire** that kicks off the entire official runner synchronization pipeline.

---

### The End-to-End Trigger Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[New official actions/runner release on GitHub] -->|GitHub Releases datasource| B[Renovate opens PR bumping runner_version in versions.toml]
    B -->|renovate.json applies protocol-sync label & blocks automerge| C[.github/workflows/runner-sync.yml triggered on PR]
    C --> D[prep job: ubuntu-latest]
    D -->|runner-watch diff| E[Calculates source delta from baseline]
    E -->|runner-watch triage| F[Generates protocol specs in .runner-watch/specs/]
    F -->|gh pr comment| G[Posts spec & delta summary directly on Renovate PR]
    D --> H[sync job: runner-sync host]
    H -->|mitmproxy + official runner| I[Captures new protocol wire goldens]
    I -->|runner-watch conform| J[Runs conformance test suite against Preloop]
    J --> K[Opens tiered implementation PRs for protocol deltas]
```

### 1. The Renovate Tripwire (`renovate.json`)
- **Datasource**: Watches `actions/runner` on `github-releases`.
- **Target**: Bumps `runner_version = "..."` in `versions.toml`.
- **Rules**:
  - Sets label: `["protocol-sync", "dependencies"]`.
  - Blocks auto-merge (`automerge: false`) because upstream runner changes require wire golden verification and spec review before adopting.

### 2. The Sync Workflow (`.github/workflows/runner-sync.yml`)
Triggered automatically whenever a PR modifies `versions.toml` (or manually via `workflow_dispatch` with custom `--from` / `--to` tags):

1. **`prep` job** (Runs on `ubuntu-latest`):
   - Compares the upstream runner codebase (`runner-watch diff --from <old> --to <new>`).
   - Parses code changes into protocol specs (`runner-watch triage`).
   - Comments the change summary directly onto Renovate's tripwire PR.
2. **`sync` job** (Runs on `runner-sync` host with `mitmproxy`):
   - Records wire goldens with the real binary.
   - Verifies Preloop's broker and Results Service conformance.
   - Spawns tiered draft PRs on `runner-sync/v<version>` branches for any protocol deltas.

name: runner-sync
…
jobs:
  prep:
    name: Prep runner sync (diff + triage)
…
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
…
      - name: Upload triage artifacts
…
        with:
          name: runner-sync-prep
          path: |
            .runner-watch/delta.json
            .runner-watch/triage-summary.json
            .runner-watch/specs/**
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  sync:
    name: Runner sync (record-golden + conform + tiered PRs)
    needs: prep
    # vars-only gate: the preloop dogfood CI evaluates job-level `if`s, so a
    # needs-outputs condition here would leave the job queued forever on that
    # pool; movement is instead detected in a step below.
    if: vars.RUNNER_SYNC_HOST_WORKSPACE != ''
    runs-on: [self-hosted, runner-sync]
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      HOST_WORKSPACE: ${{ vars.RUNNER_SYNC_HOST_WORKSPACE }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          lfs: true
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@52699249a776424c51ebc9ee197baf0f9dbf0d8a
      - name: Detect runner_version movement
        id: moved
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MOVED=true
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ]; then
            if git diff --quiet "$BASE_SHA" -- versions.toml \
                || ! git diff "$BASE_SHA" -- versions.toml \
                     | grep -q '^[+-]runner_version'; then
              MOVED=false
            fi
          fi
          echo "moved=$MOVED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Resolve versions
        id: versions
        if: steps.moved.outputs.moved == 'true'
        env:
          INPUT_FROM: ${{ github.event.inputs.from }}
          INPUT_TO: ${{ github.event.inputs.to }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          OUT="$(python3 scripts/resolve-runner-versions.py \
            --from "$INPUT_FROM" \
            --to "$INPUT_TO")"
          FROM="$(printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | sed -n 's/^from=//p')"
          TO="$(printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | sed -n 's/^to=//p')"
          echo "from=$FROM" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "to=$TO" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Init runner-watch config
        if: steps.moved.outputs.moved == 'true'
        run: cargo run -q -p runner-watch -- init || true
      - name: Diff upstream tags
        if: steps.moved.outputs.moved == 'true'
        env:
          VER_FROM: ${{ steps.versions.outputs.from }}
          VER_TO: ${{ steps.versions.outputs.to }}
        run: cargo run -q -p runner-watch -- diff --from "$VER_FROM" --to "$VER_TO"
      - name: Triage delta into specs
        if: steps.moved.outputs.moved == 'true'
        run: cargo run -q -p runner-watch -- triage --no-agents
      - name: Implement specs (agents)
        if: steps.moved.outputs.moved == 'true' && vars.RUNNER_SYNC_AGENTS == 'true'
        run: cargo run -q -p runner-watch -- implement
      - name: Review implementations (agents)
        if: steps.moved.outputs.moved == 'true' && vars.RUNNER_SYNC_AGENTS == 'true'
        run: cargo run -q -p runner-watch -- review
      - name: Record official goldens
        if: steps.moved.outputs.moved == 'true'
        env:
          VER_TO: ${{ steps.versions.outputs.to }}
        run: cargo run -q -p runner-watch -- record-golden --runner "$VER_TO" --non-interactive
      - name: Replay against the built server
        if: steps.moved.outputs.moved == 'true'
        env:
          VER_TO: ${{ steps.versions.outputs.to }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 benchmarks/conformance/check_corpus.py || true
          cargo build --quiet -p preloop-runner-server
          STATE_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/runner-sync.XXXXXX")"
          SERVER_LOG="$STATE_DIR/server.log"
          REPLAY_PORT="$(python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0)); print(s.getsockname()[1]); s.close()')"
          REPLAY_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$REPLAY_PORT"
          SERVER_PID=""
          cleanup() { [ -n "$SERVER_PID" ] && kill "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
          trap cleanup EXIT
          PRELOOP_PUBLIC_URL="$REPLAY_URL" \
            PRELOOP_CONFIG="$STATE_DIR/config.toml" \
            PRELOOP_REGISTRATION_POLICY="permissive" \
            ./target/debug/preloop-server serve --listen "127.0.0.1:$REPLAY_PORT" \
            --state-dir "$STATE_DIR/server-state" >"$SERVER_LOG" 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          for _ in $(seq 1 600); do
            kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { cat "$SERVER_LOG" >&2; echo "replay server exited" >&2; exit 1; }
            curl -fsS "$REPLAY_URL/healthz" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
            sleep .1
          done
          curl -fsS "$REPLAY_URL/healthz" >/dev/null || { cat "$SERVER_LOG" >&2; echo "replay server not ready" >&2; exit 1; }
          cargo run -q -p runner-watch -- conform --runner "v$VER_TO" \
            --preloop-url "$REPLAY_URL" --skip-cargo-test
          kill "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          SERVER_PID=""
          trap - EXIT
          echo "conform: PASS"
      - name: Open tiered sync PRs
        if: steps.moved.outputs.moved == 'true'
        env:
          VER_TO: ${{ steps.versions.outputs.to }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh auth setup-git
          git config user.name "preloop-sync[bot]"
          git config user.email "preloop-sync[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          BRANCH="runner-sync/v$VER_TO"

          # Renders the tiered PR bodies and updates versions.toml / README /

          cargo run -q -p runner-watch -- pr --dry-run
          git add -A
          if ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
            git commit -m "chore(runner-sync): reconcile actions/runner v$VER_TO"
            git push origin "$BRANCH"
          fi

**The agent code is implemented in `runner-watch`, but the environment variables and runner host are not enabled yet.**

Here is the exact state:

---

### 1. How the Agent Implementation Works (`runner-watch`)
The agent pipeline is built directly into `crates/runner-watch`:
- **Implementer (`runner-watch implement`)**: Uses `codex exec <prompt>` (configurable via `agents.implement`) to implement each generated protocol spec in `.runner-watch/specs/<version>/`.
  - Runs in a loop up to `max_implement_iterations` (default: 10).
  - Automatically runs `cargo check` and relevant tests after each iteration. If compile/tests fail, it feeds the compiler/test error back into the agent prompt to retry.
  - Automatically commits passing implementations per spec.
- **Reviewer (`runner-watch review`)**: Uses `claude` (configurable via `agents.review`) to review implementation diffs against upstream protocol semantics.

---

### 2. Current Configuration Status in the Repo

| Component | Status | Location / Details |
|---|---|---|

Layer 5  whole-repo behavior   ~28 real-world repos, 39-scenario benchmark

and the machine-readable captures in `.runner-watch/`.

`actions/runner` binary and a control plane, using a mitmproxy addon

**Yes, exactly.** The workflow is designed specifically for Preloop's execution model and will run cleanly without queue stalls:

### 1. How Preloop handles `runner-sync.yml`
* **`prep` job (`runs-on: ubuntu-latest`)**:
  * Runs on Preloop's standard Linux microVM runner pool (or GitHub-hosted).
  * Executes the deterministic diff (`runner-watch diff`) and triage (`runner-watch triage --no-agents`).
  * Posts the spec summary comment to Renovate's tripwire PR and attaches the `.runner-watch/specs/**` artifacts.
* **`sync` job (`runs-on: [self-hosted, runner-sync]`)**:
  * Gated with a root-level condition: `if: vars.RUNNER_SYNC_HOST_WORKSPACE != ''`.
  * Because Preloop evaluates job-level `if` expressions at workflow submission time, when `RUNNER_SYNC_HOST_WORKSPACE` is unset, Preloop **skips `sync` immediately** rather than letting it sit queued indefinitely waiting for a labeled runner.

### 2. Summary of our workflow states in self-hosted CI

| Workflow | Trigger / Runner | Behavior in Preloop |
|---|---|---|
| **`ci.yml`** | PRs / Main (`runs-on: ubuntu-latest`) | Standard test & lint suite across microVM pool |
| **`smolvm-release-verify.yml`** | Renovate smolvm bumps (`runs-on: [self-hosted, smolvm-host]`) | Active (gated by `SMOLVM_VERIFY_HOST_WORKSPACE=/opt/actions-runner`) |
| **`runner-sync.yml` (`prep`)** | Renovate runner bumps (`runs-on: ubuntu-latest`) | Runs automatically, diffs upstream, and posts specs on the PR |
| **`runner-sync.yml` (`sync`)** | Needs-gated downstream (`runs-on: [self-hosted, runner-sync]`) | Cleanly skipped until a dedicated MITM capture runner is provisioned |

how long does it take for renovate to open the pr?

For the hosted GitHub App (Mend Renovate):

### 1. Typical Timeline
* **Scheduled pass**: If waiting passively, Renovate scans repositories on its queue roughly **every 1 to 2 hours** (usually within 30–60 minutes).
* **On push/merge to `main`**: When a commit lands on the default branch (e.g. merging the `renovate.json` fix), GitHub delivers a `push` webhook to Renovate. Renovate prioritizes default-branch pushes and typically queues the scan **within 1 to 5 minutes**.

---

### 2. What you'll see first
1. **Dependency Dashboard Issue**: Renovate first opens or updates an issue titled `Dependency Dashboard` listing all detected packages (`actions/runner`, `smol-machines/smolvm`, cargo crates, etc.).
2. **The Bump PRs**: Immediately alongside the dashboard, it opens the PRs (e.g. `smolvm_golden_version: 1.8.2 -> 1.13.1`).

---

### 3. Forcing / Speeding it up
Once the **Dependency Dashboard** issue is opened, Renovate includes a checkbox:
> `[ ] Check this box to trigger a Renovate run immediately`

Checking that box triggers a worker pass on demand without waiting for the next cron cycle.

When working in the preloop repo (or any repo whose CI runs on the preloop

Before pushing a branch or creating a PR:

1. **Submit the workflow to the preloop server first** — this is the
   push-to-server path, and it runs the checks without the webhook round
   trip:
   ```sh
   PRELOOP_SYSTEM_TOKEN=<token> \
     cargo run -p preloop-runner-client -- --server <server> submit \
     -W <workflow.yml> --workspace-root <repo> --repository <owner/repo>
   ```
   `<server>` is the preloop control plane (e.g. `https://aksh.preloop.dev`
   or `http://127.0.0.1:9090` for a local `just serve`); the native API
   token comes from the server's `AKSH_SYSTEM_TOKEN`/`PRELOOP_SYSTEM_TOKEN`
   (local default: `preloop-system-token`). Equivalently, `POST
   /api/v1/runs` with the workflow YAML. This also snapshots the local
   workspace so reusable workflows and the submitted file resolve against
   the current tree.

2. **Create PRs as drafts** (`gh pr create --draft`) unless the user asks
   for a ready PR, and show the full title/body in chat before creating
   (see ts-show-before-create).

3. **Never draft dependency-bump PRs yourself.** Runner (`runner_version`)
   and SmolVM (`smolvm_golden_version`) bumps are Renovate's job — it opens
   the PR once `renovate.json` is on the default branch and the app is
   installed, and the verify/sync workflows gate it. Hand-simulating those
   PRs is a failure; leave them to the bot.

Push-and-wait-for-webhook is the fallback for when the preloop server is

Upstream GitHub released **`v2.337.0`** on 2026-08-26, while `versions.toml` is currently pinned to `2.336.0`:

| Dependency | Current in `versions.toml` | Latest Upstream | Renovate Action |
|---|---|---|---|

| **`actions/runner`** | `2.336.0` | `2.337.0` | Opens bump PR $\rightarrow$ triggers `runner-sync.yml` |

---

### What will happen when Renovate runs:
1. **Renovate opens the runner bump PR**:
   - Updates `runner_version = "2.337.0"` in `versions.toml`.
   - Labels it `protocol-sync` (and blocks auto-merge).
2. **`runner-sync.yml` triggers automatically** on the PR (due to the `paths: [versions.toml]` trigger).
3. **The `prep` job executes**:
   - Clones upstream `actions/runner` at `v2.336.0` and `v2.337.0`.
   - Runs `runner-watch diff` to identify all protocol and worker changes.
   - Runs `runner-watch triage --no-agents` to generate the `.runner-watch/specs/2.337.0/` spec set.
   - **Comments the full spec summary and delta breakdown directly on Renovate's tripwire PR**.

name: ci
permissions:
  contents: read

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Keep push-triggered checks observable while the self-hosted pool boots.
  pull_request:
    # Docs-only PRs must not burn pool time: skip when every changed file
    # is a markdown document.
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
  schedule:
    # Nightly intensive property profile at 02:00 UTC
    - cron: "0 2 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      profile:
        description: "Property profile: fast (default) or intensive"
        required: false
        default: "fast"


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Property-test CI notes
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PR / push: fast profile — 256 cases for pure/model/runner, 64 for HTTP.
# Scheduled / manual intensive: release mode, 10k cases, 100k shrink iters.
#
# The regular Linux jobs never run live GitHub or privileged official-runner
# probes. `runner-conformance.yml` runs the privileged deep runner probe on the
# dedicated smolVM self-hosted pool for every pull request.
# The differential harness dry-run (credential-free) runs in both profiles.
#
# Sleep-guard: each property-test job mechanically scans new test files for
# `sleep(` and fails the build if any match is found.
#
# Zero-filter guard: `cargo test -- --list | grep <filter>` must return at
# least one test name before case-count runs are launched.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

jobs:
  rust:
    # Runs on the preloop self-hosted pool: the product's own runner is the
    # CI executor (dogfood).
    runs-on: self-hosted
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      # 2 parallel debug rustc + GNU ld links peak ~4.6 GiB in the guest
      # (measured on the pool, 2026-08-13); the 5 GiB VM ceiling is the
      # floor. Unbounded parallelism OOM-killed the host once; the ceiling
      # must stay above the build peak or the guest OOM-kills rustc.
      CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: "2"
      # The dedicated property job carries the 256-case profile. Keep this
      # workspace gate aligned with `just test-ci` and bound libtest
      # concurrency so the dogfood VM survives preloop-runner's suite.
      PROPTEST_CASES: "8"
      RUST_TEST_THREADS: "2"
      RUSTFLAGS: "-C link-arg=-fuse-ld=lld"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Conformance goldens are LFS-tracked; without this they arrive
          # as pointer stubs and every test that reads them fails.
          lfs: true
      - name: Materialize conformance goldens
        run: |
          git lfs pull --include=".runner-watch/golden/**"
          fixture=".runner-watch/golden/v2.335.1/06-multi-step/flows.jsonl"
          test -s "$fixture"
          if grep -q '^version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/' "$fixture"; then
            echo "LFS fixture was not materialized: $fixture" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c
        with:
          toolchain: "1.97"
          components: rustfmt,clippy

      # inline run steps work against preloop
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@49a0bdc70d2e1b713ca9e2869b211fcce03d3c1c

      # Runner executes as root in the pool VM; sudo's audit plugin fails on
      # the mis-owned /etc/sudoers in the golden, so call apt directly.
      - name: Install lld linker
        run: apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends lld

      - run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - run: |
          # Run clippy on warning-free crates with strict -D warnings
          cargo clippy --locked -p preloop-gha-protocol -p preloop-gha-parser -p preloop-gha-expressions -p preloop-cache -p preloop-artifacts -p runner-watch -p preloop-conformance --all-targets -- -D warnings
          # Run clippy on crates with pre-existing warnings without -D warnings
          cargo clippy --locked -p preloop-runner -p preloop-runner-server -p preloop-runner-client -p preloop-dap --all-targets
      # cargo test (libtest) measured faster than nextest on this pool:
      # nextest's per-test process model cost ~4 min of spawn overhead on
      # 1628 fast unit tests (exec 17.5-18.0 min vs libtest 13.4 across
      # -j2x2, -j2x1, and serial configs). Keep libtest.
      - run: cargo test --locked --workspace
        env:
          RUSTFLAGS: "-A warnings -C link-arg=-fuse-ld=lld"

  # Bounded property-test profile
  property-tests-fast:
    runs-on: self-hosted
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Conformance goldens are LFS-tracked; without this they arrive
          # as pointer stubs and every test that reads them fails.
          lfs: true
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c
        with:
          toolchain: "1.97"

      # Zero-filter guard so just fail if no properties match the filter
      - name: Verify concurrency_properties filter matches at least one test
        run: |
          count=$(PROPTEST_CASES=1 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'concurrency_properties' || true)
          if [ "$count" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: filter 'concurrency_properties' matched zero tests in preloop-runner-server" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "concurrency_properties: $count test(s) found"

      - name: Verify property filters match tests
        run: |
          server=$(PROPTEST_CASES=1 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec 'concurrency::properties|concurrency_properties|concurrency_http_properties' || true)
          runner=$(cargo test -p preloop-runner -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'timespan_tests' || true)
          parser=$(cargo test -p preloop-gha-parser -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'concurrency_' || true)
          if [ "$server" -eq 0 ] || [ "$runner" -eq 0 ] || [ "$parser" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: zero matching tests (server=$server runner=$runner parser=$parser)" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Check no sleep() in property test files
        run: |
          files="crates/preloop-runner-server/src/concurrency_properties.rs crates/preloop-runner-server/src/concurrency_http_properties.rs"
          bad=0
          for f in $files; do
            if [ -f "$f" ] && grep -q 'sleep(' "$f"; then
              echo "ERROR: sleep() found in $f" >&2
              bad=1
            fi
          done
          if [ "$bad" -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
          echo "Sleep guard: OK"

      # Pure properties (256 cases)
      - name: Pure concurrency properties
        run: |
          PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server \
            'concurrency::properties' -- --test-threads=1
          PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server \
            concurrency_properties::pure -- --test-threads=1

      # Scheduler model properties (256 cases)
      - name: Scheduler model properties
        run: |
          PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server \
            concurrency_properties::state_machine -- --test-threads=1

      # Expression / parser properties (256 cases)
      - name: Expression and parser properties
        run: |
          PROPTEST_CASES=256 cargo test -p preloop-gha-expressions -- --test-threads=1
          cargo test -p preloop-gha-parser concurrency_ -- --test-threads=1

      # Runner dispatcher properties (256 cases)
      - name: Runner dispatcher properties
        run: |
          cargo test -p preloop-runner timespan_tests -- --test-threads=1

      # HTTP sequence properties (64 cases — heavier)
      - name: HTTP sequence properties
        run: |
          PROPTEST_CASES=64 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server \
            concurrency_http_properties -- --test-threads=1

      # Differential harness dry-run (credential-free)
      - name: Differential harness dry-run (schema + algebraic validation)
        run: |
          python3 benchmarks/real-world/run-concurrency-property-probes.py \
            --dry-run \
            --corpus benchmarks/real-world/concurrency-property-cases.json

      - name: Differential harness rejects contaminated fixture
        run: |
          set +e
          python3 benchmarks/real-world/run-concurrency-property-probes.py \
            --dry-run \
            --corpus benchmarks/real-world/fixtures/contaminated-case.json
          status=$?
          set -e
          if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: harness did not reject contaminated fixture (expected nonzero exit)" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Contamination rejection: OK (exit $status)"

      # Upload regression seeds on failure
      - name: Upload proptest regressions
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: proptest-regressions-fast
          path: |
            crates/**/proptest-regressions/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # Intensive scheduled / manual profile
  property-tests-intensive:
    runs-on: self-hosted
    timeout-minutes: 120
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.profile == 'intensive')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Conformance goldens are LFS-tracked; without this they arrive
          # as pointer stubs and every test that reads them fails.
          lfs: true
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c
        with:
          toolchain: "1.97"

      # Zero-filter guard
      - name: Verify concurrency_properties filter matches at least one test
        run: |
          count=$(PROPTEST_CASES=1 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'concurrency_properties' || true)
          if [ "$count" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: filter 'concurrency_properties' matched zero tests" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Verify property filters match tests
        run: |
          server=$(PROPTEST_CASES=1 cargo test -p preloop-runner-server -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec 'concurrency::properties|concurrency_properties|concurrency_http_properties' || true)
          runner=$(cargo test -p preloop-runner -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'timespan_tests' || true)

      - name: Intensive property profile (release)
        run: |

name: ci

  contents: read

  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Keep push-triggered checks observable while the self-hosted pool boots.
  pull_request:
    # Docs-only PRs must not burn pool time: skip when every changed file
    # is a markdown document.
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
  schedule:
    # Nightly intensive property profile at 02:00 UTC
    - cron: "0 2 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      profile:
        description: "Property profile: fast (default) or intensive"
        required: false
        default: "fast"

# Property-test CI notes
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Scheduled / manual intensive: release mode, 10k cases, 100k shrink iters.

# dedicated smolVM self-hosted pool for every pull request.

name: runner-conformance
permissions:
  contents: read

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
  schedule:
    # Weekly deep-runner probe (Monday 03:00 UTC). runner-light still gates every PR/push.
    - cron: "0 3 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  runner-light:
    name: Runner light conformance
    # Trusted contexts only (see server-conformance): fork PR code never
    # executes on the self-hosted pool.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: self-hosted
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Conformance goldens are LFS-tracked; without this they arrive
          # as pointer stubs and every test that reads them fails.
          lfs: true
      - name: Validate runner status responses
        run: python3 benchmarks/real-world/runner-conformance.py --mode light
      - name: Upload light report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: runner-light-conformance
          path: benchmarks/compatibility/runner/behavior/RUNNER-CONFORMANCE-REPORT.md
          if-no-files-found: error

  # The deep profile builds the runner from source and boots it inside the
  # repository's pre-packed smolVM machines on the macOS/ARM64 host, so it is
  # expensive (180-min timeout) and runs only on the weekly schedule or manual
  # dispatch, never on PRs or pushes. The host-only variable is the explicit
  # opt-in: webhook CI runs inside disposable Linux guests and must not try to
  # launch nested host smolVMs. Once enabled, a missing or failed prerequisite
  # fails instead of degrading to light.
  runner-deep:
    name: Runner deep conformance
    # Schedule and manual dispatch only; PR and push events never reach this
    # job. The GH token secret is trusted-context-only by construction.
    if: (github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') && vars.RUNNER_CONFORMANCE_HOST_WORKSPACE != ''
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64, smolvm-host]
    timeout-minutes: 180
    env:
      GH_REPO: ${{ vars.RUNNER_CONFORMANCE_REPO || 'preloopdev/preloop-conformance' }}
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RUNNER_CONFORMANCE_TOKEN }}
      HOST_WORKSPACE: ${{ vars.RUNNER_CONFORMANCE_HOST_WORKSPACE || '' }}
      PRELOOP_RUNNER_HOST: ${{ github.workspace }}/target/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl/release/preloop-runner
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Conformance goldens are LFS-tracked; without this they arrive
          # as pointer stubs and every test that reads them fails.
          lfs: true
      - name: Build current PR runner for smolVM
        run: cargo zigbuild -p preloop-runner --release --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
      - name: Run deep runner conformance
        run: |
          rm -f benchmarks/compatibility/runner/behavior/conformance-{preloop,official}.jsonl
          bash ./benchmarks/real-world/batch-conformance.sh both '10[1-9]-*' '11[0-5]-*'
          python3 benchmarks/real-world/runner-conformance.py --mode deep
      - name: Upload deep report and captures
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02
        with:
          name: runner-deep-conformance
          path: |
            benchmarks/compatibility/runner/behavior/RUNNER-CONFORMANCE-REPORT.md
            benchmarks/compatibility/runner/behavior/conformance-*.jsonl
            benchmarks/compatibility/runner/behavior/vm-*.log
          if-no-files-found: error

      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RUNNER_CONFORMANCE_TOKEN }}
      HOST_WORKSPACE: ${{ vars.RUNNER_CONFORMANCE_HOST_WORKSPACE || '' }}

      - name: Run deep runner conformance

        if: always()

        with:

            benchmarks/compatibility/runner/behavior/conformance-*.jsonl
            benchmarks/compatibility/runner/behavior/vm-*.log

content.text:
name: smolvm-release-verify

# SmolVM release verification — runs the upgrade path for a candidate release
# on the real-VM host.
#
# Triggered specifically by Renovate's `smolvm_golden_version` bump PRs
# (head branches `renovate/**`, see renovate.json) and manually via
# `workflow_dispatch` with a version input. It installs the candidate exactly
# as release-golden.yml and the updater do, probes the capabilities preloop
# depends on, and boots a real microVM with the candidate (create -> start ->
# exec -> delete) to gate the bump. A green run is also the signal that the
# updater's latest-stable adoption of that release is safe: it exercises the
# candidate's templates, libkrun, and KVM/Hypervisor boot path — the surface
# that broke at 1.7.5.
#
# On non-Renovate PRs the job is skipped entirely, so unrelated PRs are
# unaffected; the gate for smolvm bumps is Renovate auto-merge, which waits
# for this check and ci.yml on its own PRs. The job additionally requires a
# smolvm-capable self-hosted runner (any OS/arch with /dev/kvm or
# Hypervisor.framework — the repo's aksh-golden-x64 KVM host, or a Mac)
# labeled smolvm-host AND SMOLVM_VERIFY_HOST_WORKSPACE set (the same opt-in
# pattern as runner-conformance.yml; webhook CI runs inside disposable Linux
# guests and must not try to launch nested host smolVMs). Runs are serialized
# through a concurrency group because the job mutates ~/.smolvm on the shared
# host. The VM smoke needs the host's virtualization and registry access for
# the pinned Ubuntu base.

on:
  pull_request:
    # Renovate's smolvm bump PRs touch versions.toml; anything else does not
    # need the upgrade-path verification. Keeps the preloop CI pool free on
    # ordinary PRs (the server honors paths filters).
    paths:
      - versions.toml
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "SmolVM release to verify (default: smolvm_golden_version in versions.toml)"
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: smolvm-host
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify smolvm release on smolvm-host
    # Renovate bump PRs only (head branches renovate/**), plus manual
    # dispatch; anything else skips entirely (the preloop server evaluates
    # root-job if conditions at submission, so nothing queues).
    if: (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || startsWith(github.head_ref, 'renovate/')) && vars.SMOLVM_VERIFY_HOST_WORKSPACE != ''
    runs-on: [self-hosted, smolvm-host]
    timeout-minutes: 120
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Detect golden-pin movement
        id: changed
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          CHANGED=false
          if ! git diff --quiet "$BASE_SHA" -- versions.toml \
              && git diff "$BASE_SHA" -- versions.toml \
                 | grep -q '^[+-]smolvm_golden_version'; then
            CHANGED=true
          fi
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Resolve candidate version
        id: resolve
        env:
          INPUT_VERSION: ${{ github.event.inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$INPUT_VERSION" ]; then
            VERSION="$INPUT_VERSION"
          else
            VERSION="$(grep '^smolvm_golden_version' versions.toml | cut -d'"' -f2)"
          fi
          [ -n "$VERSION" ] || { echo "no smolvm version resolved" >&2; exit 1; }
          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Install candidate smolvm (mirrors release-golden.yml)
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || steps.changed.outputs.changed == 'true'
        env:
          SMOLVM_VERSION: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$(uname -s)/$(uname -m)" in

# unaffected; the gate for smolvm bumps is Renovate auto-merge, which waits
# for this check and ci.yml on its own PRs. The job additionally requires a

# pattern as runner-conformance.yml; webhook CI runs inside disposable Linux
# guests and must not try to launch nested host smolVMs). Runs are serialized
# through a concurrency group because the job mutates ~/.smolvm on the shared
# host. The VM smoke needs the host's virtualization and registry access for
# the pinned Ubuntu base.

name: release-linux-runner

# macOS installs execute workflows inside Linux microVMs, so every release
# must carry the Linux `preloop-runner` binary. cargo-dist cannot cross-build
# it, so this workflow zigbuilds the bundle for both Linux guest triples and
# uploads it to the release; `install.sh` and `preloop update` place it where
# the engine looks (<prefix>/lib/preloop/runner/<triple>/).

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build-and-upload-runner-bundles:
    name: Build Linux runner bundle ${{ matrix.triple }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - triple: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - triple: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c
        with:
          # Pin the workspace toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml is 1.97); the
          # action's `stable` default does not reliably install the aarch64
          # std for the cross build (E0463: can't find crate for `core`).
          toolchain: "1.97"
          targets: ${{ matrix.triple }}

name: release-linux-runner

# macOS installs execute workflows inside Linux microVMs, so every release
# must carry the Linux `preloop-runner` binary. cargo-dist cannot cross-build
# it, so this workflow zigbuilds the bundle for both Linux guest triples and
# uploads it to the release; `install.sh` and `preloop update` place it where
# the engine looks (<prefix>/lib/preloop/runner/<triple>/).

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build-and-upload-runner-bundles:
    name: Build Linux runner bundle ${{ matrix.triple }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - triple: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - triple: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@08c6903cd8c0fde910a37f88322edcfb5dd907a8 # v5.0.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@4360b52568e2003a75bf9bc1d59f33a8e3fc893c
        with:
          # Pin the workspace toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml is 1.97); the
          # action's `stable` default does not reliably install the aarch64
          # std for the cross build (E0463: can't find crate for `core`).
          toolchain: "1.97"
          targets: ${{ matrix.triple }}

        uses: goto-bus-stop/setup-zig@abea47f85e598557f500fa1fd2ab7464fcb39406

          cargo zigbuild --release \
            --target "$TRIPLE" \
            -p preloop-runner

          cp "target/$TRIPLE/release/preloop-runner" \
            "dist/preloop-runner-$TRIPLE"

          TAG_NAME: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
          TRIPLE: ${{ matrix.triple }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "$TAG_NAME" \
            "dist/preloop-runner-$TRIPLE" \
